threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just 'the train'. Also, the way you search for parking like it's an Olympic sport.
I saw a guy on the 50 bus confidently singing opera at 2am, the whole bus just went silent, then clapped when he finished. Pure Brixton magic.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw a guy in a tutu arguing with his dog over a kebab at the corner of Weserstraße.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg’s raw energy on a Monday morning during the BVG strike—everyone somehow still manages to get around by bike and foot. It's chaotic, but beautifully so.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name all the taco trucks but still complain about the new coffee shop that charges $6 for a drip.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a woman arguing passionately with a pigeon at Civic Center today. Muni might be a mess, but sometimes the real drama is right on the platform.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always ask for 'tapas' but miss the incredible bocadillos at the corner bars. It's like asking for a sandwich in Paris and ignoring the croissants.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot a newcomer by their bewilderment at the local grocery store’s lack of peanut butter options. Classic dead giveaway.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still don’t know that you shouldn't refer to the Overground as 'the train.' It’s definitely a rite of passage.
Caught a guy on the 59 juggling fruit near Coldharbour Lane last night. Thought it was odd till he started handing out oranges to passengers—strangest bus ride ever.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Walking past the Uferhallen, I caught a glimpse of a street artist painting an old lamppost—underneath, the words 'Berlin bleibt bunt.' That's when it clicked.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find open-air swimming pools filling up with locals in winter just for a chilly dip. It's a true testament to our stubbornness and love for life!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they complain about Muni delays but still swear by the burritos at La Taqueria, rain or shine.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that stopped for ten minutes because a guy was trying to sell an inflatable unicorn to the driver. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about vibrant plazas, but it’s the quiet streets lined with local bakeries that capture the real charm.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they stand at the tram stop, double-checking their route as if it’s a magic trick instead of just following the signs.
